title: 白教堂的雾 — 开膛手杰克 (1888) · 抖音竖屏 3 分钟

shots.prompt: Slow dolly forward along a narrow fog-choked Whitechapel street at night, a single cast-iron gas lamp flickering amber, fog drifting in layers across the frame, wet cobblestones glistening, soot-stained brick warehouses, distant church spire; at the far end of the street a tall silhouette holding a lantern crosses the road and dissolves into the fog. No faces visible. Camera: slow push in, slight handheld drift.

Low angle looking up at a soot-blackened Victorian brick tenement at night, laundry lines swaying, a single candle-lit window on the third floor where a thin woman with grey hair in a bun draws a curtain closed; fog rolls past the chimney pots; the gas lamp below flickers. Camera: slow tilt down from the roofline to the wet street.

Extreme close-up of a gloved hand dipping a steel-nib pen into a bottle of red ink on a scarred wooden desk lit by a single candle; the nib touches cream paper and begins writing in looping Victorian script; ink bleeds slightly into the paper fibres; candle flame trembles. Camera: static macro, shallow focus, the flame flicker animates the shadows.

A stocky middle-aged carman with a thick brown moustache, flat cap and canvas work jacket walks toward camera down Buck's Row at 3:40 AM, swinging a tin lantern that throws swaying light across the brick wall; his breath fogs in the cold; he slows and squints ahead. Camera: tracking backward at walking pace, lantern light swinging.

Over-the-shoulder of the moustached carman in a flat cap as he raises his swaying lantern toward the base of a dark brick wall on Buck's Row; the light slides along wet cobblestones and lights up the hem of a dark shawl at the bottom of the frame; fog drifts between him and the wall. Camera: slow push in past his shoulder.

Medium shot: the carman Charles Cross kneels on wet cobblestones beside a dark shape hidden by fog at the bottom of the frame, holding his lantern low; a lean man in his forties, thick brown moustache, weathered face, realistic human proportions painted like a Rembrandt portrait; he slowly lifts his head toward the camera, dread in his eyes, breath visible in the cold; fog drifts past. Camera: very slow push in.

High angle looking down into a cramped Hanbury Street backyard at cold grey dawn: a dozen East Enders in dark shawls and caps crowd the narrow passage and peer past two constables at something hidden below the frame; faces varied — an old woman with a hooked nose, a bearded docker, a thin girl — muted umber and slate palette, low light, painterly. Camera: slow descending crane toward the crowd.

A tall detective inspector in his forties with a heavy dark walrus moustache, receding hairline and a long grey overcoat steps out of a tenement back door into a cramped yard at grey dawn, takes off his bowler hat and looks slowly around at the crowd and the wet fence; Rembrandt chiaroscuro, realistic proportions, muted palette, painterly. Camera: slow descend to his eye level.

Close-up of the inspector's gloved hand resting on a rough wooden fence, rainwater dripping from the slats; slow rack focus from his hand to a row of grimy back windows where several different faces — a young girl, an old man with a clay pipe, a woman with a lace cap — watch silently from behind the glass, breath fogging the panes. Camera: rack focus, then slow pan across the windows.

Top-down shot of a Central News Agency desk under a green-shaded lamp: a clerk's ink-stained hands with rolled shirt sleeves open a cream envelope and unfold a sheet of paper; the paper is blank cream with a few blurred red ink smudges bleeding into the fibre, no legible writing; a cup of cold tea and a brass letter-opener beside it. Camera: slow push in on the paper.

A young clerk with round wire spectacles, neat side-parted blond hair and a starched collar reads the red-ink letter under a green-shaded desk lamp; his eyebrows rise, he glances nervously over his shoulder toward a dark doorway, then back at the page; the lamp flame flickers. Camera: slow push in on his face.

A Victorian steam printing press in a dim brick pressroom: giant iron rollers and flywheels turn, sheets of newsprint flow over the drum in a rhythmic blur, sparks of gaslight on oily metal, a printer's silhouette pulls a lever, folded papers stack up in the foreground; no legible writing, texture only. Camera: slow lateral dolly along the machine.

A freckled newsboy of about ten in an oversized cap and patched jacket stands under a gas lamp on a foggy street corner shouting the news, mouth open, one arm raised high out of frame, breath steaming; well-dressed passers-by in top hats turn toward him, one hands over a coin; fog and gaslight, muted palette. Camera: slow push in on the boy.

Berner Street at one in the morning: a small brown pony pulling a costermonger's cart suddenly shies and rears at a pitch-black gateway, the bearded costermonger in a wide-brimmed hat hauls on the reins and stands up on the cart; realistic horse anatomy, fog and one gas lamp, wet cobblestones, muted palette, painterly. Camera: slow push in from street level.

Continuous lateral tracking shot along a fog-filled London street at night: gas lamps pass one by one like halos, blurred silhouettes of two policemen with lanterns hurry the other way, wet cobblestones reflecting amber light, brick walls sliding by; muted umber and slate palette, painterly texture. Camera: steady lateral dolly, moderate speed.

A young constable in a tall custodian helmet and rain cape, clean-shaven with a strong jaw and pale eyes, walks slowly through Mitre Square at night raising his bullseye lantern; the beam sweeps across wet cobblestones and a dark archway, then stops dead on a shape below the frame; his face freezes, his breath fogs. Camera: slow tracking beside him, then stop.

A dark tenement doorway on Goulston Street at four in the morning lit by a policeman's lantern: on the black brick wall inside the arch a faint pale smear of chalk marks — blurred, unreadable — and on the wet step below a crumpled dark rag; the lantern beam trembles across the bricks as the constable leans in; fog behind him. Camera: slow push in toward the wall.

Close-up: a gentleman's hand in a white cuff with a gold cufflink holds a wet grey sponge and wipes slowly across a black brick wall, smearing away a pale chalk smudge in the swaying lantern light; water runs down the bricks; no legible letters, just fading chalk haze; muted palette, painterly. Camera: slow push in on the hand.

Three Victorian policemen in dark capes and helmets stand under a brick archway at grey dawn, lit by a single swaying lantern: a young constable with freckles, a sergeant with grey mutton-chop whiskers, an older one with a scar through his eyebrow; realistic human proportions, faces painted in Rembrandt chiaroscuro, each face clearly different; they exchange uneasy glances as shadows swing across the wall. Camera: slow lateral dolly.

Miller's Court, a squalid brick courtyard on a grey November morning: a nervous young man of about twenty with a thin face, dark hair under a bowler hat and a worn brown coat walks to a green door marked 13, knocks twice and waits, glancing at the small broken window beside the door; realistic human proportions, painterly, muted palette. Camera: slow tracking behind him.

Close-up on the thin young man's face in a bowler hat as he leans to the small broken window pane of Miller's Court and lifts the edge of a ragged curtain with two fingers; grey morning light on his face, his eyes widen slowly, his lips part, he stops breathing; realistic human proportions, Rembrandt chiaroscuro, painterly. Camera: very slow push in on his eyes.

The thin young man in a bowler hat staggers backward from the small broken window of Miller's Court, knocks over a wooden bucket that clatters across the wet flagstones, clutches the courtyard wall and stares at the window with wide eyes; grey November light, painterly, realistic proportions. Camera: slow pull back.

A dark gallery wall in a Victorian study: a candle carried by an unseen hand moves slowly along a row of four oil portraits in gilded frames, illuminating each face in turn — a gaunt Polish barber with hollow cheeks and a short dark beard, a clean-shaven young barrister with slicked hair, an elderly surgeon with white side-whiskers, a painter with a pointed grey beard — each face clearly different, painted in Rembrandt chiaroscuro; the light lingers a moment on each face then moves on. Camera: slow lateral tracking following the candle.

The candle stops at the last gilded frame on the dark gallery wall: the canvas inside is empty, only cracked dark varnish and a faint glint of gold leaf; the flame flickers, shadows breathe across the empty canvas, a thin wisp of smoke rises. Camera: very slow push in toward the empty canvas, holding on the dark.

Inside a Scotland Yard archive lit by a single green-shaded desk lamp: a long wooden card-index drawer slides open, yellowed case files and faded ribbon-tied bundles inside; a hand in a grey sleeve lifts a folder and its pages fan open, dust motes drifting in the lamp light. Camera: slow push in over the drawer.

Extreme close-up through a round magnifying glass of the woven silk fibres of an old faded floral shawl, brown and blue threads in soft focus; the glass drifts slowly across the fabric, then the image slowly dissolves into a glowing amber double-helix of DNA drawn in fine painterly brushstrokes turning in darkness. Camera: slow drift, then slow rotation of the helix.

The same narrow fog-choked Whitechapel street as the opening: the fog thins and lifts, night turns to grey morning, gas lamps fade out one by one, and translucent ghostly silhouettes of modern pedestrians hurry through the frame in fast motion while the painted brick walls stay still. Camera: locked-off, slow time-lapse feel.

The empty foggy Whitechapel street at dusk: a single dark figure in a long coat and top hat stands far away under the last gas lamp, face lost in shadow; the fog slowly thickens around him until only the lamp glow remains; painterly, quiet, ominous. Camera: very slow push in, then hold.
